title: Homotopy pullback descent for quasi-representable module moduli
statement:
Use the dg-category model structure of [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], dg modules of [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution], scalar extension of [lem-coef-dg-module-base-change], and nerves and spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix a small cofibrant dg category $\mathcal C$. For a small dg category $\mathcal B$ let $\mathcal W_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal B)$ be the category of dg functors $T:\mathcal C\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ whose right $\mathcal B$-module values $T(c,-)$ are projectively cofibrant and isomorphic, in the localization at objectwise quasi-isomorphisms, to some representable $\mathcal B(-,b_c)$. Morphisms in $\mathcal W_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal B)$ are just objectwise quasi-isomorphisms. The tensor category has object pairs and tensor products of morphism complexes with the Koszul sign, and opposite reverses morphisms with this sign. For $v:\mathcal B\to\mathcal E$, postcomposition on these moduli is scalar extension on each right-module value; it is defined on these cofibrant values without further replacement and is coherent under composition by the canonical scalar-extension associators.

Suppose $\mathcal B_1\xrightarrow{p}\mathcal B_3\xleftarrow{q}\mathcal B_2$ is a diagram of small dg categories with $p$ a fibration in the stated model structure, and set $\mathcal B=\mathcal B_1\times_{\mathcal B_3}\mathcal B_2$ (the strict dg-category pullback). Then the comparison square of nerves under these extension functors is homotopy cartesian. Explicitly the canonical map
$$N\mathcal W_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal B)\longrightarrow N\mathcal W_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal B_1)\mathop{\times}^{h}_{N\mathcal W_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal B_3)}N\mathcal W_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal B_2)$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence; its compatibility homotopy is induced by the canonical isomorphism between the two composite scalar-extension functors from $\mathcal B$ to $\mathcal B_3$. Here the homotopy pullback of spaces $X\to Z\leftarrow Y$ is modeled, after replacing by Kan complexes, by $X\times_{Z,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Z)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Z}Y$.
